Subject: Evidentiary standard for willful misconduct/fraud — Order Form redline

Team / Elena — attaching the latest Order Form redline (v3) from procurement. Brightline pushed back on our proposal to limit the gross negligence/willful misconduct/fraud carve-out to conduct that is proven by a high standard of proof. They want something more actionable in the OPs clause.

Key ask: we need to agree internally on the evidentiary gating language (what counts as sufficient proof to trigger the carve-out) before I respond to Elena. Brightline's procurement requested "no subjective standards" and asked for examples.

My initial thinking: keep fraud unqualified (no cap), but require a materiality gate plus an evidentiary standard (e.g., clear and convincing evidence OR criminal conviction). We should also define a narrow list of evidence types (forensic report, signed admissions, regulatory findings) and add an "evidence protocol" schedule to the Order Form to reduce later disputes.

Please review redline and call out anything that would be a deal-breaker from sales/CS perspective. Rishi — can you sketch the legal options and risk trade-offs? Marissa — any commercial flexibility on cure periods or mutuality?

Subject: Re: Evidentiary standard for willful misconduct/fraud — Order Form redline

Looping in a quick sales perspective.

- Neutral stance on the named standard as long as it is reciprocal. Brightline's ask for "no subjective standards" is reasonable; they want predictable gates.
- Commercially we can accept a "clear and convincing" standard, but only if: (1) fraud/willful misconduct remains uncapped, (2) any evidence protocol is narrow and time-boxed (30 days to produce), and (3) we maintain a cure period for non-willful/ordinary breaches.
- If legal insists on adding criminal conviction language, that will significantly delay negotiation (procurement will push back).

My recommended language to propose to the customer: "Willful misconduct or fraud shall be established by clear and convincing evidence, which may include, without limitation, a forensic report from an independent auditor, a signed admission by an authorized representative, regulatory or criminal enforcement findings, or a final adjudication in a court of competent jurisdiction."

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Evidentiary standard for willful misconduct/fraud — Order Form redline

Sean / all — legal view and trade-offs.

1) Keep fraud and intentional misconduct outside the cap: standard industry practice and strong precedent for vendor protection. That remains our position.
2) Two levers to make language defensible: (a) evidentiary standard (preponderance vs clear and convincing vs criminal conviction), and (b) materiality/causation gate (loss must be direct/foreseeable and constitute a material breach).

My recommended formulation: "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, fraud, willful misconduct, or criminally wrongful acts by a Party (each, an "Excluded Act") shall not be subject to the liability cap, provided that the claiming Party demonstrates by clear and convincing evidence that: (i) the act was committed by an authorized individual acting within the scope of their authority; (ii) the act caused the claimed Losses; and (iii) the act rises to conduct that would be independently actionable as fraud or criminal wrongdoing."

Practical considerations: requiring a criminal conviction is often too narrow — most commercial fraud is settled civilly. But "clear and convincing" plus a short list of evidentiary categories (forensic report, unambiguous audit trail, signed admission) gives us a workable middle ground. I also want to add an evidence-protocol schedule so both sides agree on timing and permitted forensic vendors. See attached evidence-protocol-matrix.xlsx for proposed categories and timelines.

Rishi Malhotra
Deputy General Counsel

Subject: Re: Evidentiary standard for willful misconduct/fraud — Order Form redline

Thanks for the note, Sean. Brightline's legal team has reviewed v3 and we shared an annotated redline (attached). A few points from our side:

- We can accept an elevated evidentiary standard but only if the language is mutual and limited to objectively verifiable evidence. We are comfortable with "clear and convincing evidence" so long as it expressly includes independent forensic reports and documented admissions.
- We will not accept language that conditions the carve-out solely on a criminal conviction — too narrow.
- We request a mutual cure/notice process before invoking the exclusion, with a 30-day dispute resolution window and agreed forensic vendor options (mutually agreed upon or on an approved list).
- Also attaching our procurement redline: Brightline_proposed_redline.docx. Note we have proposed a narrowly tailored mutuality clause and explicit timelines for evidence exchange to avoid surfacing stale claims months later.

Elena Rivera

Thanks everyone — good progress. Quick internal summary and proposed next steps: 

- Internal alignment: We will propose "clear and convincing evidence" as the evidentiary standard. Fraud and willful misconduct remain uncapped and mutual.
- Materiality gate: include language requiring the claimant to demonstrate that the act caused the Losses and that the act constitutes a material breach.
- Evidence protocol: attach the evidence-protocol-matrix as Schedule X to the Order Form (30-day initial exchange, agreed forensic vendors list). Rishi to draft Schedule X and a short set of definitions for "forensic report," "signed admission," and "final adjudication."
- Commercial ask: Marissa to confirm whether a mutual 30-day cure window is acceptable from the sales side. If yes, we propose to trade that for the mutuality and to avoid the criminal-conviction-only language.
- Next external step: I'll send a clean proposal to Elena/Jordan with the Schedule X language and the mutuality/cure trade. If that looks acceptable we can push to term sheet signature this week.

Meeting: suggest a 30-min call tomorrow to iron out Schedule X. Options: Thu 9:30am PT or Thu 2:00pm PT — please react with availability.
